paper_sections.title: Multiple brain networks contribute to the acquisition of bias in perceptual decision-making
The neural correlates of the acquired bias in perceptual decisions
Learning signals for the acquisition of bias in perceptual decisions
The changes in functional connectivity as the bias grows

description.value: The study examined how reward-context information is learned and integrated with sensory evidence to produce bias in perceptual motion decisions, using reinforcement-learning models and fMRI.

design.value: Participants performed an event-related motion-discrimination task during fMRI in two independent reward contexts. Context cues signaled which motion-direction response would receive higher reward, and trial-wise feedback was used to model context-dependent and context-free reinforcement-learning signals.

source_definition.value: the percentage of coherently moving dots
the absolute value of the difference between the two choices from the best-fit reinforcement-learning model
the difference between expected and actual outcomes followed by a choice made in the specific context
the reward prediction error used to update action value regardless of the context

description.value: Twenty-four human participants completed the behavioral paradigm in the MRI scanner; one participant was excluded because of extreme parameter estimates in the fMRI data analysis.

recruitment_method.value: recruited through posted flyers and were prescreened

medical_condition.value: free of any self-reported neurological or psychiatric diseases

task_description.value: Participants decided whether moving dots had upward or downward global motion in two reward contexts. The context cue appeared before each trial, motion stimuli were presented briefly, responses were made with spatially congruent buttons, and reward feedback followed each response.

presentation_software.value: Matlab version 7.10.0, using the Psychophysics Toolbox extension, version 3.0.10

instructions.value: They were simply instructed to decide the motion direction on each trial in order to harvest the most reward points.

stimuli.value: Each motion stimulus was composed of 150 white dots moving inside a donut-shaped display patch on a black background. Some dots moved coherently upward or downward and the others moved randomly; the stimulus was presented for 200 ms.

description.value: Functional data were collected using a T2-weighted multi-band echo-planar imaging sequence with 60° flip-angle. Forty-eight oblique axial slices were collected in interleaved fashion.

description.value: T1-weighted anatomical images were collected using an MP-RAGE sequence with 9° flip angle.

fMRI data were aligned with MCFLIRT, screened using frame-wise displacement and DVARS, skull-stripped, spatially smoothed, grand-mean intensity normalized, high-pass filtered, and registered to structural and MNI template space.

steps.value: All image time series were aligned with the MCFLIRT tool.
Frame-wise displacement and DVARS were computed to identify bad time points (FD > 0.5; DVARS > 0.5).
The skull was removed from the functional images with the brain extraction tool and from the structural images using FreeSurfer.
Spatial smoothing was applied using a Gaussian kernel of FWHM 5 mm.
The grand-mean intensity was normalized over the entire 4D dataset by a single multiplicative factor.
A high-pass temporal filtering was applied with sigma = 50.0 s.

All functional images were registered to the high resolution structural image using Boundary-Based Registration, then the high resolution structural image to the MNI-152 2 mm template using the FLIRT linear registration tool with 12 DOF.

model_settings.value: Two Q-learning models were specified: a context-dependent model in which reward prediction error updated action value for the current context, and a context-free model in which action value was updated regardless of context. A logit function generated binary choice probabilities from subjective value difference and motion coherence.

estimator.value: maximum likelihood; free parameters were fit by minimizing the negative log likelihood with nonlinear optimization

model_settings.value: The first-level model included parametric modulators for absolute coherence, trial-wise amount of bias, and reward prediction error, plus trial-evoked activity, reaction time, motion parameters, FD, DVARS, scrub regressors, and temporal derivatives. The first-level model was estimated separately for each run and participant; runs were combined within participant using fixed effects; group analysis used FLAME 1 mixed effects. Statistical maps were cluster corrected with Z > 2.3 and family-wise error corrected cluster significance P = 0.05.

Three independent PPI analyses used 10-mm spherical seeds centered on vmPFC (−6, 39, −8), left frontal cortex (−45, 21, 0), and left parietal cortex (−36, −39, 45). The PPI regressor was the interaction between the seed signal and trial-wise amount of bias.

description.value: A blue fixation-cross cue signaled one of the two reward contexts; in this context correct upward motion choices led to more reward points.
A yellow fixation-cross cue signaled one of the two reward contexts; in this context correct downward motion choices led to more reward points.
Global motion direction of the dots was upward and participants pressed the corresponding spatially congruent button.
Global motion direction of the dots was downward and participants pressed the corresponding spatially congruent button.

name.value: The neural correlates of the acquired bias in perceptual decisions: positive correlation with the amount of acquired bias

definition.value: The amount of bias acquired through reinforcement, modeled as the absolute value of the difference between the two choices from the best-fit reinforcement-learning model, positively correlates with fMRI activation.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: The amount of acquired bias has a wider influence on the perceptual decision networks, including visual and motor cortices.

name.value: The neural correlates of the acquired bias in perceptual decisions: negative correlation with the amount of acquired bias

definition.value: Negative correlation with the amount of acquired bias.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: No regions showed negative correlations with this regressor after whole-brain correction.

name.value: Learning signals for the acquisition of bias: context-based RPE

definition.value: The context-based reward prediction error regressor positively correlates with brain activation.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: The contextual RPE signals are observed in ventral striatum, frontal, and parietal cortices.

name.value: Learning signals for the acquisition of bias: context-free RPE

definition.value: The context-free reward prediction error regressor positively correlates with brain activation.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: The context-free PE signals positively correlated with activity in the visual and motor cortices when both RPE regressors were modeled together.

name.value: Context-based RPE adjusted for context-free RPE

definition.value: The RPE derived from the contextual action-outcome association positively correlates with activity after adjusting one RPE type over the other.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: The context-based RPE positively correlated with the ventral striatum, fronto-parietal cortices, and posterior and anterior cingulate gyrus.

name.value: Context-free RPE adjusted for context-based RPE

definition.value: The context-free PE signals positively correlate with activity after adjusting the context-based RPE over it.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: The context-free PE signals positively correlated with activity in the visual and motor cortices.

definition.value: The absolute value of the context-based RPE was added to account for the level of surprise.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster-based random field theory with family-wise error correction

interpretations.value: No brain regions show activation that correlates with the level of surprise after whole-brain correction.

roi_label.value: left frontal cortex; MNI coordinates X = −45, Y = 21, Z = 0; 10-mm sphere

definition.value: The interaction between the left frontal cortex seed region and the trial-wise amount of bias.

interpretations.value: Using the left frontal cortex as a single seed region, its connectivity with vmPFC, ventral striatum, and visual cortex increased as bias grew.

interpretations.value: The task-related interaction between vmPFC and left motor cortex increases as the amount of bias increases over the experiment.

caption.value: The parameter values are shown as median and the interquartile range (25th, 75th percentile) across participants. Also shown are the proportions of participants whose data are better fit by each of the learning model. Bold fonts, the best-fit model; N, the number of participants; AIC, Akaike's Information Criterion.
